description: Certified dominance comparisons for literature-based SOTA frontiers. A better result must be no worse in every recorded dimension and strictly better in at least one, on the explicit parameter domain. Comparisons are global and do not depend on active filters. Missing comparisons mean unknown or incomparable, not SOTA. Universal constant bounds are compared only at their advertised asymptotic level; parameter-dependent bounds retain their full functions. Parameter substitutions require an explicit certificate. No certificate discards an exact round count or an unresolved parameter-dependent tradeoff.

conditions.problem: Both solve unweighted minimum dominating set by selecting every vertex.
conditions.graphClass: Every K1,t-minor-free graph has maximum degree at most t−1. The larger comparison class is maximum degree ≤ t−1, not all general graphs with a uniform factor t. For t ≥ 4 the containment is strict: a subcubic tree with t leaves contains K1,t as a minor while its degree is at most t−1. For t=2 or t=3 the two classes coincide.
conditions.approximation: On maximum-degree-(t−1) graphs, the general Δ+1 bound is at most t, matching the excluded-star guarantee.
conditions.rounds: Both use exactly zero communication rounds, with no parameter-dependent overhead.

dominance.reason: The excluded-star zero-round baseline is a specialization of the zero-round maximum-degree baseline. It has no separate frontier advantage for t ≥ 4 once the larger maximum-degree class is instantiated at Δ ≤ t−1. At t=2 or t=3 the classes coincide, so this is equivalence rather than strict dominance.

conditions.approximation: Substituting ε=(log Δ)^−c gives exactly the corollary’s ratio 2+(log Δ)^−c.
conditions.rounds: This is the same Algorithm 1, not a comparison of unrelated hidden constants. In Theorem 2 the substitution makes log(1/ε)=c log log Δ and yields O(log Δ/log log Δ) for fixed c; the bounded-degree cases use the same protocol.

conditions.benchmark: Both compare the integral cover cost with weighted integral OPT.

dominance.reason: The special accuracy point is already contained in the full Theorem 2 family, with identical algorithm, guarantee and round complexity after substitution and a strictly larger accuracy domain.

conditions.problem: Both return an integral minimum-weight vertex-cover approximation on the original graph.
conditions.graphClass: Both apply to all general graphs.
conditions.approximation: The approximation ratio is identical for every allowed accuracy value; the exact-2 comparison has no additive loss.
conditions.rounds: Write x=log Δ and L=log(2/ε). The newer bound is O(x/log x+L+min{x,L x^0.001}); the older is O(x/log x+L x/(log x)^2). For sufficiently large x, x^0.001≤x/(log x)^2, so the new bound is no worse uniformly. For Δ=n and ε=1/n it is O(log n) instead of O(log² n/log² log n), giving a strict joint-parameter improvement. Bounded-degree cases are O(L) in both.

conditions.benchmark: The newer guarantee is at least as strong as the older integral-OPT benchmark. In the approximate case its proof also bounds cost against fractional OPT.
conditions.assumptions: Both use positive polynomially bounded integer weights. The older algorithm requires global Δ or a polynomial upper bound; the newer one can use local edge-degree bounds. No additional global input is introduced.
